A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MarS-FM research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original tetrapeptide and MD-Cath experiments, sampling-time measurements, sample-budget analyses, and supplementary 320 K evaluations.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds dynamical diagnostics, sampling and MSM sensitivity experiments, and structural-validity measurements.

M1.justification: The MSM-conditioned training pairs, velocity-network architecture, flow-matching objective, hierarchical sampling, and hybrid MDGen procedure remain unchanged. The expanded explanations of empirical state mixtures and per-domain MSMs match procedures already documented in v1's appendices.

E1.justification: Both evaluate tetrapeptides and MD-Cath protein domains at 450 K and 320 K. The added diagnostics and sensitivity experiments use these existing datasets and conditions; they do not introduce another population, domain, or generation task.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain MDGen-200/-1000 for tetrapeptides and MDGen-20/-100, their parallel variants, BioEmu, and the MD oracle for MD-Cath. The new analyses reuse existing comparison methods without changing membership in the retained comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 adds torsion-autocorrelation and relaxation-time evaluation, native-contact/GDT-TS divergences, covalent-geometry metrics, and controlled branching-factor and MSM-discretization sweeps. It also changes the stated tetrapeptide MSM lag from 100 ps to 2 ns in Section 5.1 and the optimizer from AdamW to Adam in Appendix B.4. These are reported setting revisions; the PDFs do not establish whether the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendices C.2, C.4, C.5, and C.7 examine fine-grained dynamical fidelity, hierarchical branching sensitivity, dependence on MSM cluster count and lag, and structural validity. These substantially extend v1's sample-budget analyses, illustrative samples, and lower-temperature evaluation.

E5.justification: Existing five-inference-run reporting and associated uncertainty values are retained. The new branching and validity tables extend that reporting practice; neither version introduces seed disclosures, confidence intervals, significance tests, or a documented increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: The original result tables retain their numerical entries, including the relocated appendix tables. v3 adds substantial results in Tables 5, 6, and 8 and Figures 7–8. For example, Figure 7 reports standalone MarS-FM backbone/sidechain relaxation correlations of 0.29/0.31, versus 0.77/0.99 for MDGen-1000. Table 8 newly reports MarS-FM bond RMSZ of 12.62 versus the oracle's 2.23. These are additional findings, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v3 introduces mathematical definitions for the added diagnostics: torsion autocorrelation and its relaxation threshold, hard-threshold native-contact fraction, GDT-TS, and bond/angle RMSZ. The underlying MSM definition, transition equations, flow-matching mathematics, and interpolation schedule remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: MSM Emulators instantiated by MarS-FM, efficient exploration, generalization across dissimilar proteins, and large sampling speedups. The main contribution paragraph is clarified without changing those claims' scope.

C2.justification: Section 4 explicitly limits fine-grained dynamical fidelity and explains complementarity with MD-Emus. New appendix discussions interpret branching-depth tradeoffs, MSM sensitivity, and structural validity versus exploration. Some interpretations are inconsistent with the evidence: C.2 claims shorter MarS-FM relaxation times, whereas Figure 7 mostly places them above the MD identity line.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-availability link and specifies inference through torchdiffeq's dopri5 solver, absolute/relative tolerances of 10^-6/10^-3, and 50 integration steps. It also revises the documented optimizer and tetrapeptide lag. Most architecture, batching, hardware, and runtime information was already present; the solver information alone does not establish a changed inference implementation.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting validity metrics, including Best et al., Chen et al.'s MolProbity work, Engh–Huber, and Zemla, and replaces the AdamW reference with Kingma and Ba's Adam reference. The main positioning relative to MD emulators, Boltzmann generators, and ensemble models remains stable. Consolidating the Flow Matching preprint/publication references does not represent a new cited work.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites in Sections 3–4.1 clarify state-conditioned sampling, per-domain MSM construction, and the role of lag time. v3 also corrects wording, updates affiliations and terminology styling, and adds an LLM-usage statement. Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a substantially different document template, including a branded title/abstract panel, changed typography, spacing, and table placement. It adds two multi-panel dynamical figures and three analysis tables. Existing visual evidence is largely retained, including v1 Figure 7 as v3 Figure 9 and the renumbered supplementary result tables.

improvement.justification: The added sensitivity tests, physical and dynamical diagnostics, explicit fidelity limitation, and solver/code information make the unchanged method more assessable and reproducible. These gains are tempered by inconsistencies in the new interpretation: Figure 7 conflicts with C.2's shorter-relaxation claim, and Table 6 shows standalone folding-energy MAE worsening from 1.05 to 1.21 at 100 ns despite C.5 claiming improvement. The additional evidence is useful, but these unresolved discrepancies limit the overall quality gain.
